models_evaluated: AI-powered DPP lifestyle intervention (mobile app with Bluetooth-enabled scale)

links.outcome: Composite of weight loss, physical activity, and HbA1c outcomes for AI-led vs human-led DPP in a noninferiority RCT
links.effect: Primary outcome achieved by 58/183 (31.7%) AI-led vs 59/185 (31.9%) human-led; risk difference -0.2% (1-sided 95% CI, -8.2%), meeting the noninferiority criterion.
links.quote: The primary outcome was achieved by 58 of 183 participants (31.7%) in the AI-led DPP group and 59 of 185 (31.9%) in the human-led DPP group (risk difference, -0.2% [1-sided 95% CI, -8.2%]), meeting the criterion for noninferiority.

screen.reason: Pragmatic randomized clinical trial evaluating the clinical effectiveness of an AI-powered lifestyle intervention vs human coach in prediabetes, without testing specific deployment safeguards or guardrails.
